paper.title: Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging and 2-year Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Mild Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: A Multicenter Study.
paper.abstract: Background Mild hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) comprises approximately 30%-50% of neonatal encephalopathy cases, yet neurodevelopmental outcomes remain difficult to predict using clinical assessment alone. Purpose To develop and externally test a diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI)-based machine learning model for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes in neonates with mild HIE. Materials and Methods This prospective four-hospital study consecutively enrolled neonates from November 2019 through November 2023, with 24-month follow-up completed in November 2025. The primary outcome was adverse neurodevelopment at 24 months, defined as any Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, third edition, composite score below 85; cerebral palsy; or epilepsy requiring ongoing treatment. Clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical-imaging models were developed from 49 DKI parameters and seven clinical variables. Model discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and curves were compared with paired DeLong tests and false discovery rate adjustment. Results Overall, 740 neonates were included (mean gestational age, 38.3 weeks ± 1.3 [SD]; 404 [54.6%] female). Adverse outcomes occurred in 182 of 510 development cohort participants (35.7%) and 80 of 230 external test set participants (34.8%). In the external test set, the combined model achieved an AUC of 0.92 (95% CI: 0.89, 0.95), with a sensitivity of 86% (69 of 80) and specificity of 85.3% (128 of 150). It exceeded the clinical-only model (AUC, 0.85; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .004) and imaging-only model (AUC, 0.86; false discovery rate-adjusted P = .005). Prespecified risk stratification yielded a negative predictive value of 100% (61 of 61) for low-risk infants and a positive predictive value of 88% (38 of 43) for high-risk infants. Conclusion In neonates with mild HIE, a combined clinical and DKI model demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes than did clinical-only or imaging-only models. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article.

paper.title: Life of a shortcut: how shortcuts can hide in embeddings during the training and testing of AI.
paper.abstract:
Purpose: AI can poorly generalize due to the model relying on "shortcuts" rather than on actual clinical task characteristics. Shortcuts are often overlooked during initial development of the AI model and result in test sets with the same biases and shortcuts that are present in the training set, leading to misleading performance levels of the AI models. Here, we present a two-stage "matching" method to detect potential shortcuts.
Methods: We trained a DenseNet121 model on the binary task of distinguishing between social vulnerability index (SVI) groups from patient chest X-rays. We evaluated it on an initial internal test set, and then on an external set from other institutions using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) as the figure of merit. We used (i) a transfer learning approach to assess whether shortcut features were included and (ii) our matching method to evaluate the impact of these shortcuts on the model.
Results: The SVI AI model achieved AUC (95% confidence interval) of 0.89 [0.85, 0.93] and 0.83 [0.77, 0.89] on an internal test dataset and an external test set, respectively. We identified features related to eight potential shortcuts related to acquisition protocols and physical artifacts. After our matching method, we obtained AUC of 0.73 [0.67, 0.79] for the model when tested on the matched set and an AUC of 0.92 [0.89, 0.95] when tested on an unmatched set.
Conclusion: These findings demonstrate the benefit of uncovering shortcuts within AI models that could have otherwise been erroneously hidden.

paper.title: An interpretable XGBoost model for predicting measured teicoplanin plasma concentrations in ICU patients with bloodstream infection: a two-center real-world validation study.
paper.abstract:
Background: Profound pharmacokinetic variability complicates individualized teicoplanin therapy in critically ill patients with bloodstream infection. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting teicoplanin plasma concentrations in this population.
Methods: This retrospective two-center real-world study included 260 intensive care unit patients from one center as the modeling cohort (randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and 91 patients from an independent center as the external validation cohort. Ten ML and deep learning algorithms were constructed using demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables. The optimal model was interpreted via Shapley additive explanations (SHAP).
Results: The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the most favorable point estimates. On the internal test set (n = 52): the model yielded an R2 of 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.81), RMSE of 3.22 (95% CI 2.62-3.77), MAE of 2.52 (95% CI 1.98-3.10), and ±30% prediction accuracy (P30%) of 78.8% (95% CI 67.3-88.5). On the external validation cohort (n = 91), it achieved an R2 of 0.76 (95% CI 0.69-0.80), RMSE of 3.61 (95% CI 3.08-4.14), MAE of 2.89 (95% CI 2.48-3.35), and P30% of 69.2% (95% CI 59.3-78.0). After Holm-Bonferroni correction, paired bootstrap comparisons showed XGBoost significantly outperformed 5 of 9 comparator algorithms in the internal test set and 7 of 9 in the external cohort, with performance comparable to several other tree-based ensemble methods. SHAP analysis identified daily dose, hemodialysis, and mechanical ventilation as features positively associated with predicted teicoplanin concentrations.
Conclusion: This internally and externally validated interpretable XGBoost model delivers consistent cross-cohort performance, and serves as a dose-anchored adjunct to conventional therapeutic drug monitoring, providing a preliminary methodological foundation for exploring individualized teicoplanin dosing strategies.

paper.title: Weakly supervised computational pathology for prognostic stratification in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma: a multicenter external validation study.
paper.abstract:
Introduction: Accurate prognostic stratification remains challenging in locally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (LA-NPC), as conventional clinicopathological factors provide limited precision for individualized risk assessment. Although hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) contain abundant morphological information, their prognostic potential in LA-NPC remains underexplored using computational pathology approaches.
Material And Methods: Patients with stage III-IVA LA-NPC from three Chinese tertiary centers were allocated into a training cohort, an internal validation cohort, and an independent external test cohort. A CLAM-inspired attention-based multiple-instance learning (MIL) model was developed using pretreatment H&E-stained WSIs and externally validated. The model was compared with four alternative MIL architectures incorporating different feature extractors and pooling strategies. Prognostic performance for 3-year progression-free survival (PFS) was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis, the concordance index (C-index), Kaplan-Meier analysis, decision curve analysis, and Cox regression.
Results: A total of 253 patients contributing 265 WSIs were included: 149 patients/160 WSIs in the training cohort, 52 patients/53 WSIs in the internal validation cohort, and 52 patients/52 WSIs in the independent external test cohort. In the internal validation cohort, the CLAM-inspired Attention MIL model yielded an AUC of 0.883 (95% CI, 0.762-0.969) and a C-index of 0.802 (95% CI, 0.705-0.884) for predicting 3-year PFS. In the external test cohort, the model achieved an AUC of 0.721 (95% CI, 0.573-0.849) and a C-index of 0.710 (95% CI, 0.591-0.819). The model significantly stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups in both cohorts and showed numerically higher AUC and C-index estimates than the four comparative MIL architectures. The risk score was linked to an elevated risk of progression (HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.06-1.60; P = 0.0126).
Conclusions: A weakly supervised CLAM-inspired Attention MIL framework can extract prognostically relevant information from routine H&E-stained WSIs and provide externally validated risk stratification for patients with LA-NPC. This approach may complement conventional clinicopathological assessment and facilitate individualized prognostic evaluation in precision oncology.

paper.title: EffNetV2M-ViT: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for MRI-Based Differentiation of Glioblastoma and Brain Metastasis.
paper.abstract: Noninvasive differentiation between glioblastoma (GBM) and brain metastasis (BM) remains challenging because of substantial overlap in their MRI appearance. Existing deep learning (DL) approaches have primarily relied on either convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which capture local spatial features, or transformer-based models, which capture long-range contextual relationships. However, the complementary value of combining these representations for GBM-BM discrimination has not been sufficiently investigated, using independently validated multicenter data. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer (ViT) framework for automated differentiation of GBM from BM. The framework integrates EfficientNet-based convolutional feature extraction with ViT-based global feature modeling through parallel fusion. Enhancing tumor was automatically segmented using 3D U-Net, with segmentations visually reviewed and manually corrected when necessary. T2-weighted (T2W) and contrast enhanced T1-weighted (CE-T1W) MRI sequences were used as inputs. A modality ablation study was performed to identify the optimal contrast combination among T1W, CE-T1W, T2W, and FLAIR. The framework was evaluated in a retrospective cohort of 344 patients with histologically confirmed tumors using cross-validation and ensemble methods, with performance further assessed in an independent multicenter external validation cohort from different institutions, MRI scanner platforms, and patient populations. The hybrid EffNetV2M-ViT framework achieved an accuracy of 95.4%, F1-score of 96.2%, and AUC of 98.4% on the internal test set, and 90.9%, 92.7%, and 96.8% on external validation, with sensitivity, specificity of 96.2%, 93.9% and 90.5%, 91.7%, respectively. The hybrid model outperformed the standalone CNN and ViT models across both datasets, with the largest performance gains observed in the external validation cohort, support its generalizability. Ablation analysis confirmed that the paired CE-T1W + T2W input yielded the most consistent performance across both cohorts, with additional contrasts providing no added benefit. These findings suggest that combining local convolutional features with global contextual representations improves automated GBM-BM discrimination, offering a noninvasive, standardized approach for MRI-based tumor classification that may support clinical decision-making.

paper.title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for predicting ICU prognosis in critically ill patients with invasive pulmonary aspergillosis: a multicenter study.
paper.abstract:
Introduction: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) is associated with elevated mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients. Early prognostic risk stratification is of great importance; however, validated clinical tools remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate an interpretable machine-learning (ML) model to predict ICU mortality in critically ill patients with IPA.
Methods: This multicenter study included a retrospective derivation cohort (n = 267, 2015-2025) and an independent prospective external validation cohort (n = 129, 2022-2025) of critically ill patients with IPA diagnosed per modified AspICU (BM-AsperICU) algorithm. Using baseline clinical features acquired within 24 h of initial IPA diagnosis, we evaluated 11 individual ML algorithms and 9 ensemble models to predict ICU mortality. Performance was assessed via area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) provided interpretability. Optimal cut-off-based risk stratification and subgroup validation were further conducted.
Results: Overall ICU mortality reached 59.1% and 53.5% in training and external validation cohorts, respectively. Eleven key features-age, interstitial lung disease (ILD), cumulative glucocorticoid dose (prednisone-equivalent, 7 days prior to IPA diagnosis), neutrophil count, platelet count, blood urea nitrogen, total bilirubin, D-dimer, PaO2/FiO2 ratio, lactate, and serum galactomannan-to-lymphocyte ratio-were selected. The logistic regression (LR) model yielded the best overall performance, achieving an internal AUROC of 0.740 (95% CI 0.626-0.840) and an external AUROC of 0.798 (95% CI 0.714-0.868) and was well-calibrated. Using an optimal cutoff of 0.54, the model identified effective prognostic stratification; high-risk patients exhibited a significantly higher ICU mortality risk, independent of age and baseline SOFA score (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.00, 95% CI: 1.07-3.70, P = 0.030).
Conclusions: Based on real-world multicenter data, our interpretable LR model and proof-of-concept web calculator enable early prognostic risk stratification upon IPA diagnosis. Further large prospective studies are required to evaluate implementation and clinical utility.

paper.title: Multimodal Integration of Imaging and Pathological Features for Postoperative Outcome Prediction in Liver Cancer.
paper.abstract: This study aimed to construct and externally validate a multimodal radiopathomic fusion model for predicting postoperative recurrence in patients with primary liver cancer (restricted to hepatocellular carcinoma, excluding intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and mixed-type hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma) after curative hepatectomy, and to explore its independent prognostic efficacy and clinical utility. A total of 280 primary liver cancer patients from two centers were retrospectively allocated to a training cohort (n = 182) and an independent validation cohort (n = 98). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative abdominal MRI, while pathomic features were quantified from H&E-stained whole-slide images. Eight machine learning algorithms were screened via fivefold cross‑validation for unimodal model development. The optimal random forest classifier was applied to construct unimodal radiomic‑only and pathomic‑only models, whereas the final multimodal fusion model was built using logistic regression with concatenated pre‑screened radiomic and pathomic features. ROC, SHAP, Kaplan-Meier survival, and logistic regression analyses were conducted to assess model performance, risk stratification, and independent predictors. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the two cohorts. We extracted 3390 MRI radiomic and 1039 pathomic features and then built single-modal and fusion models. The fusion model outperformed unimodal models (AUC = 0.894 training, 0.858 validation). It stratified patients into low-/high-recurrence risk subgroups (HR = 9.93 and 5.32). Multivariable analysis confirmed Fusion_Risk score (HR = 18.73) as the strongest independent recurrence predictor, superior to routine clinicopathological biomarkers. The radiopathomic fusion model showed good calibration and satisfactory net clinical benefit. Compared with unimodal models, it exhibited a trend toward improved predictive performance, suggesting potential value as an independent prognostic tool for individualized postoperative recurrence surveillance in patients with primary liver cancer after curative resection.

paper.title: A Multimodal large language model-based triage tool for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures using posture and movement videos.
paper.abstract: Osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture (OVCF) is common yet frequently underdiagnosed due to nonspecific symptoms and limited access to definitive imaging. We developed a two-stage screening framework that integrates prompt-guided multimodal large language model (LLM) feature extraction with machine-learning classification. In a multicenter cohort of 204 participants (102 OVCF, 102 controls), standardized posture images and functional videos were processed using pose estimation. A multimodal LLM, guided by structured prompts, generated quantitative scores for alignment, symmetry, movement coordination, and pain response. These scores, combined with clinical variables, were used to train multiple classifiers. On geographically independent external validation (n = 56), the Gradient Boosting model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.838 (95% CI: 0.712-0.940), sensitivity of 89.3%, and specificity of 71.4%, with negligible internal-to-external AUC degradation (ΔAUC < 0.001). Predicted probabilities were well-calibrated (Brier score 0.168 on external validation), and post-hoc isotonic recalibration further reduced miscalibration in the extreme-probability tails (Brier 0.151, expected calibration error 0.041) while preserving discrimination. Score-explanation concordance analysis revealed Pearson correlations exceeding 0.97 for three of six evaluated indicators. Furthermore, differential vocabulary analysis confirmed that the LLM spontaneously generated clinically coherent language distinguishing OVCF from control narratives. This framework translates home-captured posture and movement data into interpretable quantitative features, enabling accurate triage of symptomatic OVCF without direct imaging. The approach could prioritize those at high probability for confirmatory imaging and timely intervention in community and primary care settings.

paper.title: Radiological and pathological integration predicts the efficacy of bevacizumab with chemotherapy in colorectal cancer liver metastases.
paper.abstract: The differential response of patients with unresectable colorectal cancer liver metastases to bevacizumab plus chemotherapy highlights the urgent need for high-specificity predictive biomarkers. Recent studies suggest that pretreatment contrast-enhanced abdominal CT can noninvasively predict subtypes of liver metastases resistant to bevacizumab-based combination therapy. However, it remains unclear whether integrating intelligent radiological imaging with computational pathology can further enhance predictive performance while simultaneously improving the model's interpretability and elucidating the underlying mechanisms of bevacizumab resistance. Here, we developed a machine learning-based integrative model that combines abdominal CT radiomics with deep learning-based computational pathology to predict the efficacy of bevacizumab combination therapy. Using a multi-center cohort of 319 patients, we allocated patients to the following cohorts: training (n = 120), internal test (n = 50), external test (n = 47), transcriptomic validation (n = 14), and pathological validation (n = 88). The model demonstrated robust predictive performance across all cohorts. Radiomic analysis identified peritumoral features as the most significant contributors. Model interpretation using paired transcriptome data linked therapeutic resistance to inflammatory cancer-associated fibroblasts. Both deep learning-based histopathological analysis and single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed their pro-angiogenic activity. By integrating features derived from radiographic and histopathological data, we developed a dual-omics model to improve predictive performance and enable efficacy-based stratification. Collectively, our study established an integrative predictive model that combines imaging radiomics and histopathological profiling, thereby elucidating tumor microenvironment heterogeneity associated with therapeutic outcomes. This finding provides practical insights into developing non-invasive biomarkers to characterize the tumor's drug-resistant microenvironment.

paper.title: A multi-class gastric biopsy artificial intelligence model developed from whole slide histopathological images.
paper.abstract: Pathological diagnosis of biopsies remains the gold standard for gastric diseases such as gastric carcinoma (GC), but it suffers from clinical misdiagnosis and high workload. Accurately distinguishing early-stage GC (EGC) from advanced-stage GC (AGC) and preoperatively predicting lymph node metastasis (LNM) are crucial for precise treatment; however, this remains a challenge in biopsies. To address these challenges, we retrospectively collected 20,711 whole-slide images (WSIs) from 17,086 patients across six centers and prospectively enrolled 3698 WSIs from 2965 patients to develop and validate a gastric biopsy artificial intelligence model (GBAIM), which performed six-class classification on WSIs. GBAIM achieved 96.1% sensitivity and 95.0% specificity in external cohorts, and 93.4% and 99.0% in the prospective cohort, respectively, demonstrating excellent performance and strong generalization ability. GBAIM enhanced the performance of all nine pathologists in auxiliary diagnostic experiments, raising their accuracy by 1.7%-39.0%, while reducing diagnostic time by 29.4%-50.5%. Besides, the fine-tuned GBAIM-T, which aims to differentiate EGC from AGC, achieved an AUC of 0.907 and 0.826 on internal and external testing sets, respectively, and GBAIM-N, which aims to predict LNM, achieved an AUC of 0.814 and 0.706 on internal and external testing sets, respectively. Taken together, GBAIM is a valuable tool in clinical practice.

paper.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted screening of major depressive disorder using routine laboratory tests across multicenter cohorts.
paper.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent psychiatric condition with substantial personal and societal impact, yet its identification in large-scale populations still relies primarily on symptom-based clinical assessment. We introduce MD3S (Major Depressive Disorder Detection System), an artificial intelligence-assisted screening framework for identifying individuals with documented MDD using routinely collected laboratory and clinical information. Leveraging over 180,000 real-world health assessment records from the UK Biobank, MD3S integrates hematological, biochemical, and physiological indicators to distinguish individuals with MDD from non-MDD controls in a retrospective multicenter setting. To evaluate cross-population generalizability, we further validated the framework in two independent external hospital-based cohorts. MD3S achieved an accuracy of 86.57% on the internal validation dataset and maintained robust performance across two independent external validation cohorts. Compared with conventional machine learning and deep learning approaches, MD3S demonstrates improved predictive performance, stable cross-cohort transferability, and high computational efficiency. These findings highlight that routine laboratory data may support scalable AI-assisted screening strategies for identifying individuals with MDD across diverse clinical and population settings.

paper.title: Predicting Ischemic and Bleeding Risk in Patients on DAPT After PCI: A Machine Learning Model.
paper.abstract:
Background: Dual antiplatelet therapy after coronary stenting prevents ischemic complications but increases bleeding risk. Individualized assessment of these combined risks may inform treatment strategies.
Objectives: This study sought to develop a machine learning algorithm for clinical outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with potential to support clinical decisions around antiplatelet therapy.
Methods: Data from 11 clinical trials encompassing 19,106 patients who underwent PCI with everolimus-eluting stents were randomly split 3:1 to train and validate 2 separate machine learning algorithms for ischemic (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or stent thrombosis) and bleeding (Bleeding Academic Research Consortium type 3 or 5) risk prediction at 1 year. The Boruta algorithm was used to select the top 11 variables (providing >80% of predictive information) for final model development. An independent cohort of 10,696 patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary-care center (Mount Sinai Hospital) was used for external validation.
Results: There were 594 (4.1%) ischemic and 448 (3.1%) bleeding events in the training data set. Random survival forest was selected as the best-performing model (mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.76 for ischemic events and 0.81 for bleeding). Internal and external validation yielded a mean time-dependent area under the curve of 0.72 and 0.70 for ischemic events and 0.72 and 0.71 for bleeding, respectively. The 2 models met the prespecified performance goal in both validation cohorts.
Conclusions: A machine learning-based tool exhibited good discriminative ability for the prediction of ischemic and bleeding events at 1 year post-PCI and warrants prospective evaluation in clinical decisions surrounding antithrombotic therapies.

paper.title: Pulmonary Function Estimation from Opportunistic Chest CT Using a Hybrid Image-plus-Quantitative-Feature Deep Learning Model.
paper.abstract:
Background: Spirometry is underused and most airflow obstruction remains undiagnosed. Chest CT acquired for lung cancer screening contains anatomical and densitometric information that may proxy lung function.
Research Question: Can a deep learning model combining volumetric CT with CT-derived quantitative features estimate spirometric parameters and detect abnormal spirometry in independent external cohorts without retraining?
Study Design And Methods: A three-dimensional convolutional neural network trained on 10,371 low-dose CT reconstructions from 5,975 National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) participants was fused with 20 lung densitometry and tracheal geometry features to predict FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. The frozen model was applied to an External Lung Cancer Screening Cohort (ELCSC, n = 268) and COPDGene (n = 10,302 scans). Ablation, two spirometric-pattern subgroups and prevalence-conditional predictive values were also evaluated. Reference spirometry was pre-bronchodilator in NLST and post-bronchodilator in COPDGene. Abnormal spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 80% or FVC < 80% predicted) was assessed with sensitivity, specificity and AUROC, and agreement with the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC).
Results: The model detected abnormal spirometry with AUROC 0.898 (sensitivity 89.9%, specificity 66.1%) in the ELCSC and AUROC 0.913 (sensitivity 66.9%, specificity 96.3%) in COPDGene, with CCCs of 0.80-0.88 for FEV1, FVC and FEV1/FVC. In held-out development data, CCCs were 0.86/0.85/0.71 (full model) versus 0.83/0.82/0.50 image-only and 0.55/0.65/0.35 feature-only. Agreement was lower, with systematic overestimation, in a COPD subgroup (FEV1/FVC < 0.70; CCC 0.62) and in a low-FVC, preserved-ratio pattern (CCC 0.70-0.78).
Interpretation: The model estimates spirometric parameters and detects abnormal spirometry across independent cohorts without retraining, with different sensitivity-specificity profiles at the same decision rule. It shows promise for opportunistic assessment of existing CT scans, but referral performance varies by population and prospective utility is unproven.
Clinical Trial Registration: COPDGene, ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT00608764.

paper.title: Machine learning classification of depression across three population cohorts using clinical, lifestyle, and multi-omics data.
paper.abstract:
Background: Depression is one of the leading global health issues, affecting over 280 million people. The etiology of depression is complex and multifactorial. The amalgamation of these diverse factors may yield valuable predictive insights, which are instrumental in formulating strategies for the prevention, early diagnosis, and timely intervention of depression.
Methods: This study developed and validated machine learning-based models for depression risk prediction and classification using data from three cohorts: the UK Biobank (UKB), the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The integrated features included clinical data, lifestyle factors, and omics data (proteomics and metabolomics). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity. SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) was used for model interpretation.
Results: The models demonstrated solid discrimination performance across all three cohorts (AUC: 0.73-0.79), and cross-cohort validation yielded test AUCs of 0.68 and 0.71. SHAP-based feature importance analysis revealed that economic factors, marital status, physical activity, and sleep duration were core predictors across populations, while risk factors such as education level and drinking status showed significant national differences. Although the multi-omics model did not significantly improve discrimination performance, it provided new insights into the biological mechanisms of depression.
Conclusion: This study developed an interpretable machine learning framework for large-scale depression screening, offering valuable insights for the development of personalized public health interventions and clinical strategies. It holds promise for improving treatment outcomes for depression patients through earlier referral for diagnostic confirmation and population-level screening.

paper.title: Deep Learning-Derived Cardioembolism Probability from Diffusion-Weighted Imaging Predicts Occult Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Multicentre Validation.
paper.abstract:
Background: The Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment (TOAST) classification remains the dominant framework for ischaemic stroke aetiology, yet inter-observer agreement rarely exceeds κ 0.6. Deep learning algorithms trained on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) have shown retrospective promise, but prospective multicentre validation is lacking.
Methods: We conducted a prospective diagnostic accuracy study across nine stroke centres in Korea. Consecutive patients with acute ischaemic stroke who underwent DWI within seven days of onset were enrolled between May and September 2023. A commercially deployed convolutional neural network classified each case into four modified TOAST categories (large-artery atherosclerosis [LAA], small-vessel occlusion [SVO], cardioembolism [CE], and other/undetermined) and generated a continuous CE probability score. The reference standard was site-specific expert adjudication based on the complete diagnostic workup.
Results: Among 617 patients (mean age 68.9 years, 62.2% male), overall agreement was 75.7% (Cohen's κ 0.643, 95% CI 0.594-0.691). CE sensitivity reached 95.5% and SVO sensitivity 90.6%. Among 426 patients without prior atrial fibrillation (AF), the CE probability score predicted newly detected AF with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.722 (95% CI 0.634-0.806). The highest-risk quintile showed an AF rate of 17.1% (number needed to screen [NNS] 5.9) versus 4.9% (NNS 20.2) in the remaining quintiles.
Conclusions: A DWI-based deep learning algorithm achieved substantial agreement with expert stroke neurologists for stroke classification. The CE probability score predicted occult AF from a single DWI sequence. This exploratory finding warrants confirmation in adequately powered prospective studies before clinical implementation.
